content.text:
Synced groups can now share a display name as long as their external ids differ. Syncing the same set of groups twice updates them in place and creates nothing the second time.

**What changed**
- **The name check** (`server/models/Group.ts:41`): a group's name only has to be unique, case-insensitively, among groups in the team with the same `externalId`. Groups without one (made by hand) form their own set, so two hand-made groups still can't share a name, and neither can two groups with the same `externalId`. A hand-made "Engineering" and a synced "Engineering" can now sit side by side, and saving either one later won't fail.
- **The syncer** (`server/commands/groupsSyncer.ts`): groups it creates now get `externalId` set to the provider's group id. Before, it left `externalId` empty, so every synced group fell under the team-wide name check.
- **Teams already stuck**: if a linked group has no `externalId`, the next sync fills it in. That moves it out of the clashing set and stops the `The name of this group is already in use` errors.

The name check still can't see rows that aren't committed yet, because it runs outside the transaction. Groups with different external ids no longer care about that.

**Tests**
- `server/models/Group.test.ts`: hand-made duplicates are rejected even when only the case differs; the same name in different teams is allowed; groups with different external ids, plus a hand-made one, can share a name and can all still be saved afterwards; the same `externalId` with the same name in a different case is rejected.
- `server/commands/groupsSyncer.test.ts`: syncing three groups with the same name creates three groups, and a second sync creates none and keeps the same group ids; old synced groups with no `externalId` get it filled in on the next sync.

**Results**
- The model, syncer and `server/routes/api/groups` tests all pass: 68 tests.
- I put the original code back temporarily to check the new tests: three of them fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files and `tsc --noEmit` reported nothing.
- I didn't run the full `scripts/check.sh` (lint plus the whole test suite) — only the tests for the code I touched.
